kjv: Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church
mine: our sister Phoebe, a deacon of the church
note: diakonos with "of the church at Cenchreae" names an office (as in Phil 1:1, 1 Tim 3:8, where the KJV has "deacons"); "servant" here hides that a woman held it.

kjv: Andronicus and Junia … who are of note among the apostles
mine: Andronicus and Junia … They are well known among the apostles
note: Both versions read the woman's name Junia (some modern editions printed a male "Junias"). The KJV's "of note among" also allows the reading that Junia was an apostle.

kjv: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen.
mine: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
note: SBLGNT prints this benediction (with the Byzantine text) and the KJV has it too; Westcott–Hort, Tregelles and NA28 omit it, following P46, P61, Sinaiticus, A, B, C. No difference between KJV and SBLGNT here; listed because the editions disagree.

kjv: Now to him (God) that is of power to stablish you … (16:25–27, printed as the letter's close)
mine: Now to him (God) who is able to strengthen you … (16:25–27, from WH, Tregelles and NA28)
note: The doxology floats in the manuscripts: after 14:23 (the Byzantine majority), after 15:33 (P46), after 16:23 (P61, Sinaiticus, B, C, D), in two places (A, P), or nowhere (F, G; apparently Marcion's text). SBLGNT leaves it out of the main text altogether; WH, Tregelles and NA28 print it here, with identical wording, and this translation follows them. The KJV's placement agrees with these editions.

kjv: the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began
mine: the mystery that was kept silent through long ages
note: chronois aioniois is "for eternal/long ages" (dative of time, as in 2 Tim 1:9); "since the world began" fixes a starting point the Greek does not name, and "sesigemenou" is "kept silent", not "kept secret".
